builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Born for the Task: Rethinking Quantum Chemistry with Foresighted Agentic Computing
summary: BORN replaces hand-configured general-purpose quantum chemistry packages with coding agents that synthesize task-specific high-performance programs, selecting algorithmic components from a predicted accuracy-runtime Pareto frontier before execution. It costs an agent-driven synthesis phase plus the infrastructure to extrapolate error from small systems and measure hardware throughputs, and the headline gains are estimated against baselines rather than measured end-to-end. Adoption can fail if small-system error extrapolation mispredicts target-scale accuracy, if runtime prediction misses actual hardware behavior, or if the reader's workloads lie outside the demonstrated Hartree-Fock-style calculations.
rationale: The technique targets quantum chemistry program synthesis rather than LLM inference or agentic ML workloads, so it is only relevant to an AI/ML engineer with constrained infrastructure if they run computational chemistry, and even then the framework is not yet available as an adoptable tool.
technique: Foresighted agentic synthesis of quantum chemistry programs

claims.statement: BORN replaces hand-configured general-purpose quantum chemistry packages with coding agents that synthesize task-specific high-performance programs, selecting algorithmic components from a predicted accuracy-runtime Pareto frontier before execution. It costs an agent-driven synthesis phase plus the infrastructure to extrapolate error from small systems and measure hardware throughputs, and the headline gains are estimated against baselines rather than measured end-to-end. Adoption can fail if small-system error extrapolation mispredicts target-scale accuracy, if runtime prediction misses actual hardware behavior, or if the reader's workloads lie outside the demonstrated Hartree-Fock-style calculations.

For a Hartree-Fock calculation with 50,024 basis functions, BORN finishes in 1.41 h on a single CPU node, 77x faster than the estimated runtime of a general-purpose baseline (9.8x with development time included); on a single GPU it matches a GPU package running on 64 GPUs for ubiquitin and shortens a B-DNA duplex calculation from an estimated two months to 8.1 h (173x).
